sanskrit: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् । विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥
hindiTranslation: शरीरको छोड़कर जाते हुए या दूसरे शरीरमें स्थित हुए अथवा विषयोंको भोगते हुए भी गुणोंसे युक्त जीवात्माके स्वरूपको मूढ़ मनुष्य नहीं जानते, ज्ञानरूपी नेत्रोंवाले ज्ञानी मनुष्य ही जानते हैं ॥
englishTranslation: The deluded do not see the inner being departing, staying, or enjoying the world through the qualities. Those with the eye of understanding do see.
essence: What changes is seen by the wise; the true self is not what moves.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Ordinary sight cannot grasp the true self moving through bodies and experiences. Only clear understanding sees what is really happening.
simpleInsight: It brings relief from identifying with every passing role, state, or sensation.
detailedMeaning: With Arjuna frozen between duty and grief, Krishna explains that the true self is hidden from ordinary perception: it seems to move, stay, and enjoy through changing bodies, and wisdom alone can recognize it.
modernRelevance: In a hospital ward, families watch the monitors and the body, waiting for change. Krishna says the departing self stays hidden from ordinary eyes, and the eye of understanding sees what is happening.
translationLiteral: उत्क्रामन्तम् (departing) / स्थितम् (remaining) / वा (or) / अपि (also) / भुञ्जानम् (enjoying) / वा (or) / गुणान्वितम् (endowed with the qualities) / विमूढाः (the deluded) / न (not) / अनुपश्यन्ति (perceive) / पश्यन्ति (see) / ज्ञानचक्षुषः (those with the eye of knowledge)
insight: The deluded miss the self leaving, staying and enjoying; those with the eye of wisdom see it.

quoteVariants.text: Delusion misses the inner being. Clear seeing knows it never leaves.
See clearly: action changes, the true self does not.
What seems to move was never what you are.
See through change. The true self remains.
